summary: p8 verifies ~3 of the 6 p7 blockers as fixed or resolved. The pools no longer radiate-starve: the close-view ground went from pure black (p99 0.0076, 0 px >0.3) to a measured p99 0.60 with 6.6% of ground pixels >0.3 and a VLM-judged 7/10 window-reflection image — the smear-tolerance + skyglow-miss fix is real. The night-floor blocker dissolves under correct measurement: with the identical linear method the actual night reference cs2_08 sits at ground p10 0.0038 / full p01 0.0010, and our frames measure at or above those — the p7 '3x too dark' verdict was anchored on a non-reproducible 0.0126 figure and LOOK_TARGET's 0.010 is a daytime target; night floors are now in-family (ground p99 0.547 vs ref 0.570) and should not be lifted further. Evidence hygiene improved: night_city with buildings shows a believable lit-window skyline, quality=medium night evidence is accepted as quality-independent, and columns rose from 1-3 to 4-6 per frame. But the two most iconic wet-night features are still missing after two rounds: not one readable red tail-light streak exists on any asphalt surface (red_ground 11-325 px vs the reference's 190k, VLM sees zero smears in full frames and dedicated 2x crops), and vehicle spray remains 0/10 in both day frames despite a second measured-bracket retune — at this point the parameter bracket is proven not to be the bottleneck. Columns are also still muddy, and pool reflections carry heavy dither noise. Score 7.5/10 (up from 7.0): fail against the 8.5 bar. Next round must (1) light the red tail path at visible amplitude — verify a tail lamp actually smears ≥40 px vertically on the mirror by measuring a column of red before shipping evidence, (2) rework spray emission/placement rather than re-tuning radiance — a visible-at-2x puff test is mandatory evidence, (3) crisp up the lamp columns and de-noise pool reflections (temporal accumulation or blur-on-mirror), (4) stop re-shooting near-duplicate street frames and attach .log.json to every frame including night_road.
